head.title: Warn when resolving an incident from the CLI leaves status page events open
head.summary: The status page commands in the ask already shipped in rootly-cli#57 (v0.6.1) as `status-pages list` and `status-pages events list/create/update/resolve`. What remains is the footgun in the title: resolving an incident from the CLI says nothing about public status-page entries still open. Add a best-effort, stderr-only warning, in its own helper package, that lists each open event with its status page and the exact `rootly status-pages events resolve <id>` command. No auto-resolve, no renames.

additions.text: Solve IR-6586 — one PR. Add status page commands to the CLI (status-pages list, status-pages incidents create/update/resolve). Ref https://github.com/rootlyhq/rootly-cli/issues/52
additions.author: operator
the operator
additions.text: Should incident resolution ever resolve open status page entries automatically (or via an opt-in flag)? → go with: No: warn only, default behaviour unchanged. Resolving a public status page entry is a customer-visible write that can notify subscribers. The ticket asks for the mismatch to be visible, not for automatic resolves. Don't add an opt-in flag in this PR either. The warning already prints the exact `status-pages events resolve <id>` command to run. Mention an opt-in flag as a possible follow-up in the PR.

criteria.text: After a successful `incidents update` that sets --status to resolved or closed, stderr lists each status-page event for that incident whose status is not resolved/completed, giving its status page ID, its status and the exact `rootly status-pages events resolve <event-id>` command (unit test with a mock HTTP server).
criteria.cites: The read check should let a script refuse to report

criteria.text: The same warning fires after `incidents create --status=resolved` and after `alerts resolve --resolve-incidents` for each related incident that is resolved or closed (tests).
criteria.cites: The read check should let a script refuse to report

criteria.text: No warning is printed when the incident has no events, all events are resolved/completed, or the command does not leave the incident resolved (tests).
criteria.cites: The read check should let a script refuse to report

criteria.text: The check is best-effort: if the events lookup fails, the command still succeeds with the same exit code, and the warning goes to stderr only, so JSON/YAML stdout is unchanged (tests).
criteria.cites: Read-only support was called an acceptable fast partial fix

criteria.text: The check lives in its own new package (internal/statuspagewarn) and each command calls it with one line; it only warns: no event is auto-resolved, no opt-in flag is added and no existing command or flag is renamed (operator answer: warn only, default behaviour unchanged).
criteria.cites: No: warn only, default behaviour unchanged. Resolving a public status page entry is a customer-visible write that can notify subscribers.

criteria.text: go test, golangci-lint and go vet pass and total coverage stays at or above COVERAGE_MIN (make coverage && make coverage-check).
The PR is opened and its body links rootly-cli#57 and issue #52 and mentions an opt-in resolve flag as a possible follow-up.

changeKindReason: Not a bug fix: the incident update works as designed; the ticket asks for visibility into a separate public action.

scopeCuts.reason: Already shipped as `status-pages events create/update/resolve` in rootly-cli#57 (v0.6.1); renaming would break released users.
scopeCuts.answer: approve: both cuts match what I already decided. (1) The requested write commands already shipped as `status-pages events create/update/resolve` in rootly-cli#57 (v0.6.1). Renaming them or adding an `incidents` alias would break released users, so no rename. (2) Resolving public status page entries automatically is a customer-visible product decision. This PR makes the mismatch visible with a warning to stderr that lists open events and the exact resolve command, and it does not resolve anything. Mention an opt-in flag as a possible follow-up.
